notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 10/20/2025
Patient: Maya Gislason, 67-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 10/20/2025. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 56.3 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 7% of all events. Sleep stages were adequately recorded, showing normal cycling through REM and non-REM phases. Oxygen saturation levels decreased during apneic events, with a nadir of 82%. These findings indicate severe sleep apnea requiring clinical intervention.

notes.title: Sleep Medicine Consultation
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/05/2026
Patient: Maya Gislason, 68-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of obstructive sleep apnea with ongoing CPAP therapy.

History:
Maya is a 68-year-old female with a diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea currently treated with CPAP. She reports consistent nightly use of her CPAP device.

Physical Examination:
BMI 25.9 kg/m2.

Sleep Study and CPAP Data:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 28.3 events/hour on CPAP at 14 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates persistent obstructive events despite adherence to CPAP therapy at an adequate pressure setting.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative treatment options including possible adjustment of CPAP settings or evaluation for advanced therapies.
2. Continue monitoring adherence and symptomatology.
3. Follow-up consultation in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Summary:
Maya Gislason remains symptomatic with significant residual apnea events on CPAP therapy. Further management strategies will be explored to improve her sleep quality and reduce apnea events.
